claims.claim: Origen of Alexandria was an early Christian theologian and ascetic who lived from approximately 185 to 253 CE.
Origen was born at Alexandria of Christian parents and became head of the Catechetical School of Alexandria, first informally and then officially in 203.
Origen's nine extant homilies on Judges were delivered sometime between 238 and 248.

The homilies expound on themes extracted from Judges 2-7, including God's redemption of Israel through judges and events such as Gideon's defeat of the Midianites, Gideon's test with the fleece, and the murder of Sisera by Jael.

Origen applies his allegorical method of Scriptural interpretation, using both allegory and typology, and draws meaning from the literal (somatic) sense as well as from the two figurative (psychic and pneumatic) senses.
The homilies call the audience to participate in a loving relationship with Christ through interaction with Scripture and brim with hope in Christ's ultimate victory over sin and death.
Pope Benedict XVI praised Origen for his 'primordial role' in the history of lectio divina, the prayerful reading of Scripture, in his General Audience of May 2, 2007.
